title: Opportunistic Fungi: Cryptococcal Induction, Hairy Leukoplakia, Aspergillus Heads and Rhizopus
summary: Learn the phased treatment of cryptococcal meningitis, how oral hairy leukoplakia differs from thrush, how to read uniseriate and biseriate Aspergillus heads (A. niger is biseriate), and how Mucorales hyphae and Rhizopus rhizoids look.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 57 High-Yield Hits 31 (cryptococcal induction), 32 (oral hairy leukoplakia vs thrush), 33 (A. niger) and 34 (Rhizopus/Mucorales). Hit 33 says A. niger has uniseriate phialides and smooth conidia; Stemler 2023 and Bian 2022 describe A. niger as biseriate, and the lesson teaches biseriate (existing register flag rv-niger-seriation). Conidial texture is not taught. Hit 31’s “fluconazole is for consolidation/maintenance” is qualified: the WHO 2022 preferred induction includes fluconazole with liposomal amphotericin B and flucytosine. Hit 32’s “thrush scrapes off” applies to pseudomembranous candidiasis; chronic hyperplastic candidiasis does not scrape off. Hit 34’s “aseptate” is taught as pauciseptate (coenocytic, sparse septa). Not taught: drug doses beyond the WHO table summary, ART timing, cryptococcal diagnosis.

objectives: Outline the induction, consolidation and maintenance phases of cryptococcal meningitis treatment.
Distinguish oral hairy leukoplakia from pseudomembranous candidiasis, and name the confirmatory test.
Identify A. fumigatus and A. niger by colony colour, head shape and seriation.
Recognise Mucorales hyphae and Rhizopus rhizoids, and contrast them with Aspergillus hyphae.

scenes.title: Four findings, one patient group
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: four findings from patients with advanced HIV or other severe immunosuppression — (1) CSF with encapsulated budding yeast, cryptococcal meningitis; (2) a white, corrugated plaque on the side of the tongue that does not come off with gentle scraping; (3) a black mould from sputum; (4) a sinus biopsy with broad, ribbon-like hyphae. Question token: “Which drug, which lesion, which mould?”

cues.text: Invented scenario. A patient with advanced HIV has cryptococcal meningitis. What is the first, induction treatment?
Another patient has a white plaque on the side of the tongue that does not come off with gentle scraping.
And the lab has two moulds: a black Aspergillus from sputum, and broad, ribbon-like hyphae in a sinus biopsy. Which drug, which lesion, which mould?

props.label: Which drug, which lesion, which mould?

scenes.title: Two kinds of hyphae
scenes.altText: Schematic: two hyphae drawn as cards. Aspergillus: narrow, regularly septate hyaline hyphae with acute-angle (dichotomous) branching. Mucorales: broad, ribbon-like, coenocytic hyphae — septa absent or sparse (pauciseptate) — with right-angle branching, invading vessels. Rhizopus card: unbranched pigmented sporangiophores bearing sporangia with an apophysis, and root-like rhizoids formed opposite the sporangiophores; Rhizopus is the most important cause of mucormycosis, most often R. arrhizus. Histopathology is the reference standard for mucormycosis.

cues.text: In tissue, Aspergillus hyphae are septate, with acute-angle, forking branches.
Mucorales hyphae are broad and ribbon-like, with right-angle branching. They are coenocytic: septa are absent or sparse, so pauciseptate is the precise word.
In culture, Rhizopus has unbranched sporangiophores with root-like rhizoids formed opposite them. Rhizopus is the most important cause of mucormycosis, most often Rhizopus arrhizus.
Histopathology showing these broad, invading hyphae is the reference standard for diagnosing mucormycosis.

scenes.title: Aspergillus heads: one row or two
scenes.altText: Definition card: uniseriate = phialides borne directly on the vesicle; biseriate = phialides borne on metulae. Species card (Stemler 2023 table): A. fumigatus — blue-green colony, columnar head, uniseriate; A. niger — black colony, radiate head, biseriate (metulae about twice as long as phialides); A. flavus — yellow-green, radiate, uni- and biseriate; A. terreus — yellow-brown to cinnamon, densely columnar, biseriate. Token: all species of Aspergillus series Nigri are biseriate (Bian 2022); the uniseriate black aspergilli are other species such as A. japonicus and A. aculeatus.

cues.text: Aspergillus is identified by its conidial head. Uniseriate means the phialides sit directly on the vesicle. Biseriate means they sit on a supporting row of metulae.
Aspergillus fumigatus forms blue-green colonies with columnar heads, and it is uniseriate.

Aspergillus niger forms black colonies with radiate heads, and it is biseriate, with metulae about twice as long as the phialides. Aspergillus flavus is yellow-green and radiate; Aspergillus terreus is cinnamon-brown and densely columnar.
A taxonomic revision found every species in the niger series to be biseriate. The black aspergilli that are uniseriate are different species, such as Aspergillus japonicus and Aspergillus aculeatus.

scenes.title: White plaques and cryptococcal phases
scenes.altText: Plaque cards: pseudomembranous candidiasis (thrush) — curdy white plaques that come off with gentle scraping, leaving a red base; oral hairy leukoplakia — white, corrugated plaque, mainly on the lateral border of the tongue, not removable by scraping, caused by productive Epstein–Barr virus replication in severely immunocompromised people, confirmed by EBV in situ hybridisation; exception token: chronic hyperplastic candidiasis also does not scrape off. Phase card (WHO 2022 preferred regimen, adults with HIV): induction = single high-dose liposomal amphotericin B plus 14 days of flucytosine and fluconazole; consolidation = fluconazole 800 mg/day; maintenance = fluconazole 200 mg/day. Hook answers card.

cues.text: Back to the tongue. Thrush, pseudomembranous candidiasis, forms curdy white plaques that wipe off with gentle scraping and leave a red base.

Oral hairy leukoplakia is a white, corrugated plaque on the side of the tongue that does not scrape off. It is caused by Epstein–Barr virus, and in situ hybridisation for the virus confirms it. Careful: chronic hyperplastic candidiasis does not scrape off either.

Cryptococcal meningitis is treated in three phases. In the 2022 WHO guideline the preferred induction is one high dose of liposomal amphotericin B with two weeks of flucytosine and fluconazole. Fluconazole alone then carries consolidation and maintenance.
Hook answers: amphotericin plus flucytosine induction, hairy leukoplakia, biseriate Aspergillus niger, and a mucormycete, most likely Rhizopus.

props.title: Hook answers
lines: AmB + flucytosine · hairy leukoplakia · biseriate niger · Rhizopus

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “A. niger is uniseriate” (✓ A. niger is biseriate; A. fumigatus is the uniseriate, columnar one); “Fluconazole alone is enough for induction” (✓ induction pairs amphotericin B with flucytosine; fluconazole alone is for consolidation and maintenance); “Every white plaque that won’t scrape off is hairy leukoplakia” (✓ chronic hyperplastic candidiasis is fixed too; confirm hairy leukoplakia by EBV in situ hybridisation).

cues.text: Trap one: Aspergillus niger is uniseriate. No: niger is biseriate. Fumigatus is the uniseriate, columnar one.
Trap two: fluconazole alone is enough for induction. No: induction pairs amphotericin B with flucytosine. Fluconazole alone is for consolidation and maintenance.
Trap three: any white plaque that will not scrape off is hairy leukoplakia. No: chronic hyperplastic candidiasis is fixed too, so confirm the virus by in situ hybridisation.

props.title: ✗ “Fixed white plaque = hairy leukoplakia.”
lines: ✓ Rule out hyperplastic Candida; EBV ISH

scenes.title: Ribbons, roots and a black double row
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Rhizopus = Roots and Ribbons at Right angles; Niger = a black head with a double row.” Tokens: Ribbons + Right angles = Mucorales · Roots (rhizoids) = Rhizopus · Black double row = biseriate niger. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: Rhizopus means roots and ribbons at right angles. Rhizoids are the roots; broad ribbons branching at right angles are the hyphae. Aspergillus niger is a black head with a double row: metulae, then phialides.

Where it breaks: Mucorales hyphae can have a few septa, other Mucorales such as Mucor can form rhizoids too, and some black aspergilli are uniseriate, so species identification may need molecular methods.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: Mucorales hyphae can have a few septa

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Cryptococcal induction = amphotericin B + flucytosine · fluconazole carries consolidation and maintenance”, “Hairy leukoplakia does not scrape off · niger is biseriate · Mucorales = broad pauciseptate right-angle hyphae”.

cues.text: Induct cryptococcal meningitis with amphotericin B plus flucytosine, remember that hairy leukoplakia does not scrape off while thrush does, and read moulds by their structures: Aspergillus niger is biseriate, and Rhizopus has broad, sparsely septate, right-angle hyphae with rhizoids.

props.label: Hairy leukoplakia fixed · niger biseriate · Rhizopus ribbons + rhizoids

explanation.what: Plain language: people with weak immune systems get infections that healthy people rarely get. Cryptococcal meningitis needs a strong two- or three-drug start and then a long tail of one drug; a white tongue patch that won’t rub off may be a virus, not yeast; and moulds are named by how their hyphae and spore heads look. Scientific terms: induction, consolidation, maintenance; liposomal amphotericin B (L-AmB), amphotericin B deoxycholate, flucytosine (5FC), fluconazole; oral hairy leukoplakia (OHL), Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), in situ hybridisation (ISH); pseudomembranous and chronic hyperplastic candidiasis; vesicle, metulae, phialides, uniseriate, biseriate, columnar, radiate; coenocytic/pauciseptate hyphae, sporangiophore, apophysis, rhizoids.
explanation.why: Induction combines fungicidal drugs to clear the CSF quickly; fluconazole alone is less effective at that stage, so it is used to consolidate and then prevent relapse until immune recovery. OHL reflects productive EBV replication in tongue epithelium of severely immunocompromised people, so it is fixed to the surface, whereas thrush plaques are loose debris of cells and yeast. Mould morphology (septa, branching angle, head structure) separates genera and species that differ in treatment.
explanation.measure: WHO 2022 preferred adult HIV regimen: single liposomal amphotericin B 10 mg/kg plus 14 days of flucytosine 100 mg/kg/day and fluconazole 1200 mg/day, then fluconazole 800 mg/day (consolidation), then 200 mg/day (maintenance). OHL: EBV ISH is the reference diagnostic test. Aspergillus: fumigatus blue-green, columnar, uniseriate; niger black, radiate, biseriate; flavus yellow-green, radiate, uni- and biseriate; terreus cinnamon-brown, densely columnar, biseriate. Mucorales: broad, ribbon-like, pauciseptate, right-angle branching; Rhizopus rhizoids opposite sporangiophores.
explanation.differs: Thrush (scrapes off) vs OHL (fixed, EBV) vs chronic hyperplastic candidiasis (fixed, Candida); uniseriate vs biseriate heads; Aspergillus (septate, acute-angle) vs Mucorales (pauciseptate, right-angle); induction vs consolidation vs maintenance.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: choose the induction regimen for HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis, name the white plaque that does not scrape off, match a described Aspergillus head to a species, or identify Rhizopus from broad right-angle hyphae with rhizoids.

points: Red base; yeast and hyphae in the debris

comparisons.distinguisher: Gentle scraping removes thrush but not OHL (or chronic hyperplastic candidiasis).

mnemonic.text: Rhizopus = Roots and Ribbons at Right angles; Niger = a black head with a double row.
mnemonic.explanation: Roots are rhizoids, ribbons are broad pauciseptate hyphae branching at right angles; the double row is metulae plus phialides (biseriate).
mnemonic.limitation: Mucorales hyphae can have a few septa; Mucor and some other Mucorales can form rhizoids; some black aspergilli (A. japonicus, A. aculeatus) are uniseriate, and species ID may need molecular methods.

analogyLimitations: Hyphae and conidial heads are shown as schematic cards, not micrographs.
Doses are the WHO 2022 adult regimen for HIV-associated disease as tabulated by Ngan 2022; other guidelines and settings differ.
takeaway: Induct cryptococcal meningitis with amphotericin B plus flucytosine, remember that hairy leukoplakia does not scrape off while thrush does, and read moulds by their structures: Aspergillus niger is biseriate, and Rhizopus has broad, sparsely septate, right-angle hyphae with rhizoids.

questions.stem: An adult with advanced HIV has cryptococcal meningitis. Which regimen is the WHO 2022 preferred induction therapy?

options.text: Single high-dose liposomal amphotericin B plus 14 days of flucytosine and fluconazole
options.rationale: Correct. This AMBITION-based regimen is the WHO 2022 preferred induction option.
Incorrect. That is the maintenance dose; fluconazole alone is not an adequate induction.
Incorrect. This is consolidation, given after induction.
Incorrect. Nystatin is not part of any WHO 2022 induction, consolidation or maintenance option.

questions.stem: A patient with HIV has a painless, white, corrugated plaque on the lateral border of the tongue that does not come off with gentle scraping. Which test best confirms oral hairy leukoplakia?

options.text: In situ hybridisation for Epstein–Barr virus on a biopsy
options.rationale: Correct. EBV ISH is regarded as the gold-standard test for OHL.

options.text: KOH preparation of a scraping showing hyphae
options.rationale: Incorrect. Candida hyphae can colonise OHL secondarily, and their presence does not establish or exclude OHL.
Incorrect. OHL is caused by Epstein–Barr virus; a fungal antigen test does not detect the virus.

options.text: No test: a fixed white plaque is always hairy leukoplakia
options.rationale: Incorrect. Chronic hyperplastic candidiasis and other keratoses are also fixed; one study confirmed only 20 of 28 clinically suspected OHL lesions by EBV ISH.

questions.stem: A sputum isolate forms black colonies. Microscopy shows radiate conidial heads with phialides borne on metulae. Which description fits best?

options.rationale: Correct. A. niger has black colonies and radiate, biseriate heads.
Incorrect. A. fumigatus is blue-green with columnar, uniseriate heads.
Incorrect. Rhizopus forms sporangia on sporangiophores, not conidial heads with metulae.

options.text: Aspergillus terreus, a densely columnar species
options.rationale: Incorrect. A. terreus is yellow-brown to cinnamon with densely columnar heads.

claims.text: Three-phase cryptococcal treatment; WHO 2022 preferred induction (single L-AmB + 14 days flucytosine + fluconazole); fluconazole 800 mg/day consolidation, 200 mg/day maintenance; fluconazole monotherapy inferior for induction.
Thrush scrapes off leaving a red base; OHL is fixed, lateral tongue, EBV-driven, confirmed by EBV ISH; chronic hyperplastic candidiasis is also fixed.

Uniseriate vs biseriate definition; fumigatus blue-green, columnar, uniseriate; niger black, radiate, biseriate; flavus and terreus features; series Nigri all biseriate; uniseriate black aspergilli A. japonicus and A. aculeatus.
Aspergillus septate acute-angle hyphae vs Mucorales broad ribbon-like pauciseptate right-angle hyphae; histopathology reference standard.
Rhizopus rhizoids opposite sporangiophores; most important mucormycosis agent, most often R. arrhizus; Mucor can form rhizoids.
Reviewer: A. niger has smooth round conidia.
claims.note: Not taught. The sources read describe conidia of series Nigri relatives as roughened to echinulate and do not support “smooth”; not verified for A. niger itself.

claims.text: Scenario invented; hyphae and heads schematic.
“Roots and ribbons at right angles; black double row.”

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 57 Hit 33 describes A. niger as uniseriate with phialides over the entire vesicle and smooth conidia. Stemler 2023 and Bian 2022 describe A. niger (and all of series Nigri) as biseriate; the lesson teaches biseriate and does not teach conidial texture (existing register flag rv-niger-seriation).

Ch. 57 Hit 31 says fluconazole is for consolidation/maintenance. That holds for fluconazole alone, but the WHO 2022 preferred induction (and several alternatives) include fluconazole alongside amphotericin B and flucytosine (Ngan 2022; Jarvis 2022) (register flag rv-crypto-induction-who2022).

Ch. 57 Hit 32 says thrush scrapes off. This is true for pseudomembranous candidiasis, but chronic hyperplastic candidiasis forms plaques that cannot be removed by gentle scraping (Vila 2020), so a fixed white plaque is not automatically OHL (register flag rv-ohl-fixed-candidiasis).

Ch. 57 Hit 34 calls the hyphae aseptate. Sources describe Mucorales hyphae as pauciseptate (coenocytic, septa sparse or irregular), and Mucor species can also form rhizoids (Gullì 2024; Walther 2019) (register flag rv-mucorales-pauciseptate).

morphology.note: No micrographs or clinical photos; hyphae, heads and lesions shown as schematic cards.

verification.notes: All 5 taught factual claims checked against open-access sources read in full text via Europe PMC (Jarvis 2022, Ngan 2022, Harrison 2023, Khammissa 2016, Martins 2017, Vila 2020, Stemler 2023, Samson 2014, Bian 2022, Silva 2011, Gullì 2024, Walther 2019). The WHO 2022 guideline itself was not read directly; its regimen is taken from the Ngan 2022 summary table. One reviewer claim (A. niger smooth conidia) is pending and not taught. No human expert has reviewed this lesson.
